name: antimicrobial resistance overview
title: Antimicrobial resistance decision chart: a resistant organism has either an enzyme that destroys the drug (penicillinase, AmpC in the SPACE organisms, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase, carbapenemase), an altered target (MRSA, penicillin-resistant S. pneumoniae, vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus, vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus), a way to keep the drug out (porins, efflux pumps) or a bypass of the blocked pathway (folate scavenging against sulfonamides); each tells you which drugs it takes out

root.title: The culture says RESISTANT: WHICH MECHANISM, and which drugs does it take OUT?
lines: antibiotics kill the sensitive bugs AND the normal flora → the few resistant ones flourish, and can pass resistance to other bacteria
which drug to use instead: see the CHOOSING ANTIBIOTICS chart

groups.title: CHANGE the target
lines: the main route in GRAM-POSITIVE COCCI

groups.title: Keep the drug OUT, or go AROUND it

head: h
β-lactamase enzymes
break the β-lactam ring
how: e.g. the SPACE organisms: Serratia, Pseudomonas, Proteus, Acinetobacter, Citrobacter, Enterobacter
out: most β-lactams, NOT carbapenems · e.g. ESBL E. coli

head: h
Altered binding site
the drug cannot bind
how: Penicillin-binding protein (PBP) or the cell wall
out: methicillin-resistant S. aureus · PBP2 → PBP2a: β-lactams cannot bind
S. pneumoniae: its OWN gene mutated

head: h
Less drug INSIDE
how: entry blocked, or the drug pumped out
out: it can use ALL four mechanisms
